title: Asian shares mostly higher tracking Wall Street gains and oil stabilizes
description: Asian shares are mostly higher tracking Wall Street gains, with South Korea's stock market, rebounding after earlier sharp losses on a tech sell-off. U.S. futures have edged up. South Korea's benchmark Kospi index gained 1.3%, while Japan's Nikkei 225 was up 0.9%. Oil prices are stabilizing after the U.S. and Iran said separately they would be sending delegations to Qatar, although Iran has denied that talks have been arranged with the United States. Brent crude, the international standard, was trading 0.2% lower at above $73 a barrel, slightly higher than pre-war levels. On Monday, Wall Street's benchmark S&P 500 added 1.2%. The Dow Jones Industrial Average climbed 0.6%, and the Nasdaq composite gained 2.1%.

description: Asian stocks are mixed on Wednesday, following a sell-off in big technology stocks from Asia to Wall Street. U.S. stock futures are also trading mixed. Global investors are monitoring market movements in Japan and South Korea, which have seen big gains in recent months on the global AI boom but both fell sharply on Tuesday. South Korea's benchmark Kospi index was up 0.5% on Wednesday, while Japan's Nikkei 225 lost 1.1%. On Wall Street, the benchmark S&P 500 fell 1.4% Tuesday. The tech-heavy Nasdaq composite dropped 2.2%, while the Dow was 0.1% lower. Oil prices fell as more ships crossed the Strait of Hormuz and as U.S.-Iran talks on a permanent end to the Iran war progressed.

description: More drops for chip stocks and other AI winners overshadowed gains for the majority of Wall Street. The S&P 500 was little changed Thursday, even though more than two-thirds of the stocks within the index rose. The Dow Jones Industrial Average climbed 1.1% to another record, while the Nasdaq composite dropped 0.8% after erasing an early gain. Stocks broadly got help from data showing U.S. hiring slowed last month. That pushed traders to trim bets for a possible hike to interest rates later this month. But chip stocks from Seoul to New York continued to slide.

title: Wall Street quietly mixed as chip companies continue to lose ground following Wednesday's sell-off
description: Wall Street was mixed in light trading early as chip stocks fell further and oil prices dipped near their levels before the Iran war began. Futures for the S&P 500 were unchanged before the opening bell Thursday, while Dow Jones Industrial futures inched up 0.2%. Nasdaq futures were off 0.4%. Shares of chipmakers were down again in premarket after a big sell-off a day earlier that saw Micron and Intel each lose between 9% and 10% of their value. Micron was down another 2.3% overnight. Oil prices fell again, touching levels not seen since the Iran war started in late February.

title: World shares are mixed, with South Korea's Kospi down nearly 8% on a sell-off of chip shares
description: Shares have slumped in Japan and South Korea in the latest spate of heavy selling of computer chip stocks. In Seoul, the Kospi index sank 7.9%, while Tokyo's Nikkei 225 lost 2.5%. Surging demand for artificial intelligence has pushed prices of related tech stocks higher, with markets in South Korea and Japan among those reaping the biggest gains. Oil prices slipped after negotiators from the U.S. and Iran met separately with mediators from Qatar and Pakistan. U.S. futures edged lower.
